_readme: Single source for the CV PDF (cv/cv.tex) and the homepage (index.html). Edit it through admin.html; a GitHub Action rebuilds both on every save. Markup: **bold**, *italic*, [text](https://link), ^{nd} for superscript. In dates, a new line becomes a line break on the PDF. show: both | cv | site. Entries: heading (bold title), org (second line, or after a comma on one-line entries), location (right-hand side, under the dates), note (after an en dash on one-line entries), url (makes the heading a link), amount and selectivity (awards: printed after the title), dates, roles (several lines under one heading: title, org, dates), projects (italic title, bullets, then a status line), bullets, table (label/text rows), prompt (a note to yourself, printed only by a profile with prompts on), id (used by profiles). _{d} is a subscript. profiles: the CVs built from this file. The one with id "cv" is cv/cv.pdf, .docx and .txt; each other one is cv/cv-ID.*. A profile takes every entry (or, if it lists tags, every entry with one of those tags) from its sections, plus "include" ids, minus "exclude" ids; descriptions: false drops bullets and tables. photo and photoAlt: a picture shown under the entry on the site's CV page. meta.headshot: a JPEG printed beside the name on CVs whose profile has headshot on. meta.ampersand: print 'and' as '&' (not in paper, talk or project titles, or quotes). Profile options: fullLink (point to the full CV on pages 2+), selected (say 'Selected' over trimmed sections), subheadings (default on).

projects.title: A novel cyclic peptide that blocks human autoimmune antibodies for the treatment of multiple sclerosis.

bullets.text: Designed cyclic peptides against multiple sclerosis autoantibodies eight-residue design scaffold & Rosetta/FlexPepDock workflow; ran molecular-dynamics simulations for my top-ranked peptide CAP8, with GROMACS simulations & alanine scanning; in the published study, CAP8 bound anti-GlialCAM autoantibody with *K*_{d} = 0.294 mM, versus 4.82 mM linear & 2.61 mM unrelated cyclic controls & cut epitope detection on Western blot by 69% versus 27% & 5% for controls.

entries.heading: Emerging Scholars Research Fellow, Early Modern Sikh History
entries.org: Harvard Sikh Center; mentor: Satnam Singh

projects.title: Dissemination and the making of Khalsa authority in a contested panth.

bullets.text: How the early Khalsa came to dominate the wider Sikh world against rival claimants, including the Bandai Khalsa, Minas, Ram Raiyas and Hindaliyas.
Argue that the answer lies less in politics than in transmission: the Khalsa’s consolidation of ‘authentic Sikh teachings’ through *katha* preceded and enabled its control of the panth.

Sources: Gurmukhi and Persian primary materials, including works attributed to Bhai Mani Singh, *hukamname*, *rahit-nama* and sampardaic literature, alongside Persian and European accounts of the period.

projects.status: Twelve-week fellowship term producing a paper and a presentation: first, a characterization of the intellectual landscape and its conflicts; second, a prosopography linking intellectual influences to the period’s political figures.

entries.prompt: Which manuscripts and editions you actually worked from, and where the argument stands at term end.

bullets.text: Trace the legal history of end-of-life decision-making from *In re Quinlan* (1976) to *Cruzan v. Director, Missouri Department of Health* (1990).
Compare how three physician-authors, Sherwin Nuland, Atul Gawande and Haider Warraich, account for dying in modern American medicine.

projects.status: ‘Independent study’ module, project complete, academic manuscript in preparation.

why.shared: Molecules and manuscripts are two different interests, but they are two sides of one coin, and that coin is who I am. University is meant to teach you how to think, and each turban I wear teaches me a different way.
why.molecules:
*I stumbled into research.* It started as a box to check on the way to medicine. In my first semester I joined a peptide lab as a math major, surrounded by chemists, with no clue what I was getting myself into. I took it seriously anyway, and **it became the career I want**.

*Not everything goes to plan.* When our lab moved to Houston, **our team kept the work going from Newark**.

*On the ambulance, medicine is about the next ten minutes. In the lab, it is about the next ten years.* **Translational medicine sits between the two**, and that is where I want to work: treating patients, and helping build treatments that reach far more than one person.
why.manuscripts:
*I stumbled into history too.* While studying abroad in Sweden, I met Satnam Singh, a Danish historian. I read his work and **wanted to add to the field myself**.

*The tools are getting extraordinary.* Soon we will design molecules faster than we can test them, and the hardest questions will not be computational: who gets these therapies, who patients trust, how we care for people at the end of life. **History helps me think about those.**

*Sikh history stays with me too,* as **a pursuit of its own**.
